confirmed_task:
Using the TVMaze episode list for show 82, consider only records whose season equals 1. Report the season-1 episode count; the name, episode number, and airdate of the first and final episodes; and the name, episode number, airdate, and average rating of every season-1 episode tied for the highest displayed average rating.

Stopping condition: Stop after the season-1 count, boundary episodes, and all highest-rating ties have been reported.

Constraints:
- Use only the supplied TVMaze episode response and records with season equal to 1.
- Use number for the within-season episode number and rating.average for ranking.
- Report every tie for the maximum non-null rating.average; do not break ties arbitrarily.
- Do not use episode summaries or records from later seasons.

items.criterion: Restrict analysis to TVMaze episode list for show 82 and season = 1 only
items.description: Uses only the supplied TVMaze /shows/82/episodes response (as provided in context) and filters strictly to records where season equals 1. Full credit if no later-season episodes or non-supplied sources are used. Partial credit if mostly season 1 is used but one or more later-season records leak into calculations or reporting. No credit if the analysis is based primarily on other sources or seasons.

Counts the number of episode records with season = 1 and reports that count. Full credit for an accurate count based on the filtered season-1 records. Partial credit if a counting method is described but the final number is off by a small margin due to an obvious mistake (e.g., off-by-one) while still using season=1 records. No credit if count includes other seasons or is missing entirely.

items.criterion: Report boundary episodes (first and final) for season 1 with required fields
items.description: Identifies the first and final episodes within season 1 (by within-season episode number) and reports for each: name, episode number (the within-season number), and airdate. Full credit if both boundary episodes are correct and all required fields are included. Partial credit if boundaries are correct but one required field is missing for one/both episodes, or if boundaries are chosen incorrectly but still from season 1. No credit if boundary episodes come from other seasons or are not reported.

items.criterion: Identify maximum non-null rating.average among season-1 episodes using rating.average for ranking
items.description: Finds the highest displayed (non-null) rating.average among season-1 episodes and uses that value as the maximum for tie selection. Full credit if the maximum is correctly determined and null ratings are excluded from maximum calculation as specified. Partial credit if the agent uses rating.average but mishandles nulls (e.g., treats null as 0 without stating) yet still largely identifies the correct top-rated set. No credit if ranking is based on another field (e.g., overall rating, votes, or summary text) or includes later seasons.

items.criterion: Report all season-1 episodes tied for highest rating with required fields (no arbitrary tie-breaking)
items.description: Reports every season-1 episode whose rating.average equals the season-1 maximum (including all ties) and for each provides: name, episode number (within-season), airdate, and rating.average. Full credit if all and only the tied maximum episodes are listed with complete fields. Partial credit if one tied episode is omitted or an extra non-max episode is included, or if one required field is missing for one episode. No credit if ties are broken arbitrarily (listing only one when multiple share the max) or if required fields are not provided.

items.criterion: Stopping condition adherence (report only requested outputs)
items.description: Stops after reporting: the season-1 count, the first and final season-1 episode details, and all highest-rating tie episode details. Full credit if no extra episodes (e.g., all season-1 episodes, later seasons) or unrequested content (e.g., summaries) are included. Partial credit if minor additional context is provided but does not add extra episodes or violate constraints. No credit if the response continues with additional seasons, full episode listings beyond the requested subsets, or uses summaries despite the constraint.
